newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco stadium bond trails in poll - paper.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco stadium bond trails in poll - paper.

text.p: A $100 million bond measure that would help build a new football stadium in San Francisco is trailing in the polls by eight points, according to a published report Monday.

About 47 percent of the voters surveyed said they oppose the stadium plan while 39 percent said they would support the project, according to a San Francisco Chronicle poll. Fourteen percent are still undecided.
The bond measure, which will appear on the June 3 ballot, calls for San Francisco to invest up to $100 million in lease revenue bonds in the proposed sports and retail complex.

The proposed stadium and retail project are expected to cost $537 million, including $250 million to build a stadium for the National Football League's 49ers and $200 million for the entertainment and shopping complex.
The Chronicle poll has a margin of error of plus or minus four percentage points.
